title: State-machine testing driver: subsumed random-sequence runner vs Hypothesis RuleBasedStateMachine
summary: Both drivers share one harness (real engine, synthetic workers, operations: worker outcomes, review outcomes, step, pause, resume, stop, gate approve/reject, retry, crash-restart that kills in-flight workers) and check the constitution section 10 invariants after every operation. Unpatched engine: 0 violations over 40 seeds x 50 ops (~2,000 checked states, hostile profile reaching review-exhaustion gates, APPROVAL_REQUIRED, BLOCKED and failed repairers). Planted mutation (engine ignores material review findings): the subsumed runner detected it at seed 3 after 18.8 s and shrank 41 ops to a 5-op sequence (resume, step, review:reject, step, step) in 78 s total; Hypothesis (60 examples x 40 steps, uniform rule weights) did not detect it in 186 s. First run of both drivers missed the mutation entirely, which exposed a vacuous invariant (FND-0008). Caveats: one mutation; Hypothesis not tuned (rule weights, example count).
